note: Facsimile copy of ms. map of Carr-Boyd's 1895 route, showing detail of route only, in W.A. Map includes waterholes, water courses, Rutler's grave, gold prospect at Minnie Creek, relief by hachures, and named features. Few of these names became official names. "Copy supplied at the request of Mr. Carr Boyd 4.1. [18]96. Vide S.G.O. 103/96" "Copy supplied to Mr. [?] and other plans 31.10 [18]95, spelling corrected. [Signed] E.P.L., CD" ie. E.P. Laurie, Chief Draughtsman. Note on original concerning accuracy of map by "C.H.H. 18/8/96" ie. Charles Hope Harris. The report on this expedition, with an edited version of the map was published in Geographic Journal, V.9, no. 1, Jan. 1897, p. 120.

note: Facsimile of tracing, with additions, of ms. map by Captain John Hutchison and Frederick Howard, June 1864, of the Adelaide River from Pt. Ayers to Mantons Hill, the fartherest point reached by the boat of the Beatrice. Map shows soundings, mileages along river, with notes on banks, obstructions in river, and some relief hachures and spot heights. This map extends to Escape Cliffs. This tracing could have been made for use by Finniss for his journey up the Adelaide River, or for Francis Cadell's surveys in the N.T. in 1867-68, which used Beatrice's maps. Photograph of an original held by the Northern Territory Archives Service. The original of this tracing was drawn as part of Finniss's 1864-65 expedition.

Photograph of an original held by the Northern Territory Archives Service. Drawing made during Goyder's expedition, by a member of his Northern Territory survey Party, 1869, or by a member of the Government Resident's Party, 1870. Photograph of an original held by the Northern Territory Archives Service.
mapTitle: Plan of the South Arm [Port Darwin, Northern Territory]
series: Explorers' plans Northern Territory

note: Facsimile of ms. map of the Daly River from Anson Bay inland ca. 30 miles. Map shows river, some detail of banks, extent of Julia's course and that of its gig, with some notes on the channel, vegetation and topography. Relief by hachures. Map extends to Daly River Mission Site, and Mount Haywood. Written on original: "Surveyor R.H. Edmunds 1867". Original has been mended with tape and some detail obscured. Photograph of an original held by the Northern Territory Archives Service. Edmunds was a surveyor in B.T. Finniss's expedition of 1864-65, asking to be invalided out for opthalmia in Nov. 1865, but not listed in party's leaving. Map may have been compiled on his return to Adelaide. The "Julia" surveyed Victoria River in Aug. 1865 and possibly surveyed the Daly River during its return Journey to Adam Bay, Sept. 1865, and was also used for River exploration undert V.T. Manton before Jan. 1867.
mapTitle: Rough eye sketch of the Daly River, Anson Bay [Northern Territory] : [surveyed from the "Julia"].
series: Explorers' plans Northern Territory

Hingston, or and enlarged tracing of Carrington and Hingston's original map, which was published 1886, for navigation purposes. Map extends from Borroloola to South West Island, showing soundings, riverbanks with depths in feet, and some notes on the course taken from original map, which are mostly illegible on facsimile. Dating: situation 1886 ; if working sketch 1886 ; if tracing, taken before the survey by Captain Stevens in 1896.

mapTitle: Exploration survey [Marshall, ie. Hay, and Field Rivers, Northern Territory]. Field sheet no. 18 : Camel traverses, lat. & long. observed with 6 transit Dec. 1905

note: Facsimile of col. ms. map extending from Daly River to Adelaide River and Adam Bay, showing tracks of Finniss, W.P. Auld, F.H. Includes the route of the "Beatrice", and notes on topography and development possibilities. The gold district is located in the Mt. Hayward-Finnis River area, Daly River Region. "Enclosure A to Tender, B.J. Finniss, Oct. 1868", map being for attachment to tender made to South Australia Government to survey the N.T. On original: "Note: The distances on this plan are all too large Mr Flint having taken his rate of travelling at 4 m. per hour instead of 3". note: Diazo prints of a set of ms. maps showing a contour survey based on aerial photographs of the Gungahlin A.C.T. area from Gundaroo Road, Palmer Hill to Mulligans Flat, southwards. Sheets index aerial photo runs, show roads, tracks, dams and buildings, with relief by contours at 5 ft. intervals and spot heights. Trig points are those of the 1:63 360 Lake George sheet, pub. 1944 and superceded in 1971. Drawn and reproduced, by 1964 and before 1977, probably by the Australian Survey Office. Maps relate to proposals for a new airport at Gungahlin to replace Fairbairn Airport, as planned by the National Capital Development Commission in its 1964 report "The Future Canberra", but which proposal was abandoned by 1975. National Library of Australia lacks sheet 3.

note: Lithograph of Walter Burley Griffin's winning design for Canberra showing his plan on a base map.  Though this was a first design map drawn in Chicago & based on a standard kit, it demonstrates the main design features of his later maps. The Land Axis from Mt. Ainslie to Mt. Bimberi forms the main design focus of the city crossed at right angles by the Water Axis [corresponding to Kings Avenue] along which followed the flood plain of the Molonglo River but which Griffin proposed to create three interconnected lakes (east, central, and west basins) with their shorelines marked by circular or straight promenades or boundary drives. The other design axis at right angles to the Land Axis corresponded to Constitution Avenue and formed the base of the National Triangle [referred to now as the Parliamentary Triangle] which here almost encompasses Capital Hill. He then based three primary city centres on the three apexes of this triangle. Griffin proposed that government buildings ought to be built on each side of the land axis on the south side of a proposed lake, rising up in a hierarchical manner towards a focal point on Capital Hill. This would form the Government Centre. The base of Capital Hill became the focus of nine intersecting avenues and form a circular, radial network of roads intended to reduce dangerously acute intersections and odd-shaped blocks - this type of layout is reproduced in other city centres. The Civic Centre [now called Civic] was placed at the northern apex of the triangle with City Hall located here to carry out administrative functions along with the post office, courts, banks, and places of business aligned along the third axis of Constitution Avenue to act as the city's high street. The black dotted line represents the railway line with the railway station located on the eastern tip of the national triangle [i.e. the suburb of Russell] forming the third centre, the Market Centre around which the markets and shops were to be located with the railway line passing underground to avoid disruptions. Other more ancillary city centres were grouped around these three axial lines such as the Education Centre established at the western end of the Water Axis with the university at the foot of Black Mountain which included botanical gardens. Griffin's modular design is based on these specialised Centres marked on the map as hexagonal or octagonal hubs of intersecting street systems and interconnected by larger radial avenues or boulevards. "No. of lith. 13.132.D." Compiled for the Federal Capital Designs Board. Relates to: Federal Capital City / Federal Capital Designs Board (P.P. no. 17, v.2, 1912)
mapTitle: [Federal Capital Design Competition premiated designs]. [Competitor no. 29, Walter Burley Griffin] : [on base map] Map of contour survey of the site for the Federal Capital of Australia

note: Map showing the flight paths of the London to Melbourne MacRobertson Race, 20 October 1934. Two flight paths, indicated by red and black and white lines, are drawn from London to Melbourne, across Europe, the Middle East and Asia. The MacRobertson Trophy Air Race took place in October 1934 as part of the centenary celebrations of the state of Victoria with a 15,000 pounds prize put up by Sir Macpherson Robertson. Black and white photographs of aircraft are located in each corner (TWA Douglas DC2 at top left, an Amstrong Whitworth XV at top right, a Vickers Vincent at bottom left and a Fairey Long Range Monoplane at bottom right). The "Trajects" printed in two boxes, with speed and handicap routes providing distances in both miles and kilometers. Includes "Amsterdam - Boekhandel G.J. Graauw - Batavia", listing racing numbers, aircrafts, engines, and pilots.
mapTitle: London Melbourne MacRobertson race, 20 October 1934.

note: Cadastral town map of Windsor, New South Wales. Shows area from Rickaby's Creek to South Creek, and from the Hawkesbury River to South Creek. Shows named streets, farming, reserves, churches, parks, cemetery, hospital, nurses quarters, railway line and station, town hall, speedway, sewage pumping station, electric sub-station, police and court house, waterworks, tannery, rivers and creeks. Signed "K. Mortley, Elec. Eng."  [George Frederick Keith Mortley (1896-1972) was the town's Electrical Engineer from 1924 until at least 1955]. Dyeline print. National Library of Australia's copy has handwritten annotations in pencil, including on rear of map: "Mr. F. J. Mason, Town Clerk, Windsor". Frank J. Mason was the Town Clerk 1927 - 1967. Estimated date based on the location of the Council Chambers (referred to as Town Hall) in its old location, in George Street opposite Christie Street intersection; in 1966 new Council Chambers and offices were constructed further down George Street.

Projection varies: Simple conical projection; Albers conical equal area projection. Published monthly with annual cumulation. From Nov. 2005 issues include a gridded key indicating total rainfall in that period measured in mm. National Library of Australia's copy dated 1911 located at MAP Daisy Bates Special Col. /98 . note: Map series showing annual general distribution of rainfall in inches over Australia, by isohyets and shading. Sheets for 1909-1929 issued under the direction of H.A. Hunt, Commonwealth Meteorologist; sheets for 1930-1939 issued under the authority of the Honorable the Minister of State for Home Affairs by W.S. Watt, Acting Commonwealth Meteorologist; sheets for 1940-1949 prepared under the instruction from the Minister for Air by H.N. Warren, Director Met. Services; sheets for 1950-1959; prepared under the instruction from the Minister for the Interior by E.W. Tincke, Acting Director, Meteorologist Services; 1960-1967 issued by Director of Meteorology; 1968-1973 issued by direction of W.J. Gibbs O.B.E., Commonwealth Director of Meteorology under the authority of the Hon. Peter Nixon M.P., Minister for the Interior; 1974-[2002] by Bureau of Meteorology. From 1995 includes side panels showing annual decile ranges. Printed on both sides from 1914. Sheets for 1963-1976 have accompanying booklets. Subtitle varies: Based on telegraphic reports only (1960-1989); Based on gridded data (1995); Based on station data (1997) National Library of Australia's copy at MAP Daisy Bates Special Col. /65 formerly held at MS 365/93/31 (1918).

note: Map series showing annual general distribution of rainfall in inches over Australia, by isohyets and shading. Sheets for 1909-1929 issued under the direction of H.A. Hunt, Commonwealth Meteorologist; sheets for 1930-1939 issued under the authority of the Honorable the Minister of State for Home Affairs by W.S. Watt, Acting Commonwealth Meteorologist; sheets for 1940-1949 prepared under the instruction from the Minister for Air by H.N. Warren, Director Met. Services; sheets for 1950-1959; prepared under the instruction from the Minister for the Interior by E.W. Tincke, Acting Director, Meteorologist Services; 1960-1967 issued by Director of Meteorology; 1968-1973 issued by direction of W.J. Gibbs O.B.E., Commonwealth Director of Meteorology under the authority of the Hon. Peter Nixon M.P., Minister for the Interior; 1974-[2002] by Bureau of Meteorology. Mercator projection statement given on sheets for 1944-1953; Albers conical equal-area projection with two standard parallels 16⁰30'S, 34⁰30'S on sheets for 1954-1989; Lambert conformal with standard parallels 10 deg S, 44 deg S on sheet for 2000. Includes notes and tables showing average rainfall over districts compared with normal district falls, shaded areas showing more than average rain fall represent slightly more than one third of the whole are of the Commonwealth, reduced maps for comparison showing areas of above average rainfall, and insets. From 1995 includes side panels showing annual decile ranges. Printed on both sides from 1914. Sheets for 1963-1976 have accompanying booklets. Subtitle varies: Based on telegraphic reports only (1960-1989); Based on gridded data (1995); Based on station data (1997) National Library of Australia's copy at MAP Daisy Bates Special Col. /65 formerly held at MS 365/93/31 (1918).

note: Reproduction of an early Dutch map of Australia and New Zealand commonly attributed to Abel Tasman but drawn originally from many sources by the Dutch East India Company inspired by Tasman's 1642 discoveries. Under orders issued by Governor General van Dieman Abel Tasman set out in 1642 to discover new lands in the southern latitudes. He first discovered Tamania (which he named Van Dieman's Land) in November 1642 on his first voyage, later discovering New Zealand as well as the Fiji Islands. In February 1644 he headed another exploratory mission as directed by the Dutch East India Company, sailing to the south coast of New Guinea to chart any coastline sited of the 'Southland'. But on their return in August 1644 no strait had been discovered south of New Guinea and no sightings of the eastern coast of Australia were reported. Nevertheless, the Dutch East India Company, drawing on Tasman's recent observations and those of previous Dutch explorers, had formed a reasonable estimation of the shape of this southern continent. Naming it 'Compagnis Niew Nederland' or the Company's New Holland, they drew up this composite map (referred to now as the Tasman Composite Chart)  featuring a sweeping hypothetical eastern coastline which is nevertheless fairly realistic. The northeast tip of Australia is the greatest discrepancy projecting as far north as New Ireland in the Bismarck Archipelago and adjoined with New Guinea. Title proper supplied by cataloguer.
mapTitle: [Australia and New Zealand] : from the original map made under the direction of Abel Tasman in 1644 and now in the Mitchell Library, Sydney

note: Topographic map series of eastern New South Wales. Relief shown by contours and spot heights. Shows topographic, cadastral and local government information. Also shows types of roads, surfaces and ground conditions. Each sheet has individual title and number. Bottom right of sheets: New South Wales standard 2 inches to 1 mile topographic map On some sheets: Provisional issue. On later sheets: Printed and published by the Department of Lands, Sydney. Some sheets overlayed in purple with cadastral information. Includes index to adjoining sheets and legend. Sheets overlayed with cadastral information also include key to local government areas. Series published circa 1958-circa 1972, with reprints of some sheets issued to 1979. Some sheets issued as "provisional issue" in monochrome, or monochrome with brown contours. Sheet names and numbers originally based on 1:63,360 sheet names and numbers, divided into quarters: e.g. Quirindi A, Quirindi B, Quirindi C, Quirindi D. Naming and numbering changed in the early 1960s to individual names for each sheet, and numbering deriving from 1:100,000 sheet numbers divided into 8: e.g 9034-I-N, 9034-I-S, 9034-2-N, 9034-2-S, 9034-3-N, 9034-3-S, 9034-4-N, 9034-4-S. Series was superseded from the early 1970s by the metric 1:25,000 scale series, which followed the same sheet numbers and names. National Library of Australia's holdings include unpublished 'field sheets' for the Young and Berridale 1:63,360 or 1:50,000 sheet areas.
mapTitle: Burraga, Sheet 8830-III-S - New South Wales Australia 1:31 680

note: Plan of Kilfera Run, County of Manara, west of Ivanhoe, New South Wales, showing paddocks with names, swamps, fencing, parish boundaries, tracks, buildings, dams, water tanks, wells, yards and roads. Total area of run 830,620 acres. The run contains the following named blocks or paddocks in the County of Manara: Amoona, Bingarah, Bonton, Bonuna, Burlabah, Caroerinyah, Casey, Coolaminyah, Gerathula, Katabritoi, Kilfera, Lyons, Manara, Marli, Martomah, Matheson, Moornanyah, Mulca, Nangutyah, Natumberah, Quambie, Thooulminah, Thumulah, Umalee, Wawilly, Whitminbah, Wokobity, Yelty. Many of the intermittent swamps marked on the map (in blue) have properties and paddocks of the same name (Giles, I tank, Goorah, Mountain tank, J well, Mulga, Hard tank, P Well, Day & night, etc). Generally ‘horse paddocks’ are located around more permanent water or wells, to allow boundary riders to swap or spell horses, and as mustering points for lamb marking and checking stock. The cleared track running diagonally through the map was cut so that station hands could find their way and to allow for easier mustering. The southern part of Kilfera Run was open plains country running into the creek country, while the northern sections are very scrubby. The Travelling stock route to the eastern side follows the old coach tracks from Balranald, to the south, and Wilcannia, to the north, possibly following Aboriginal tracks to the creek and river country. The Travelling Stock Route to the west follows mostly higher ground around the creek country, towards Menindee. Includes notes and the original manufacturer’s stamp in the upper right hand corner.
mapTitle: Plan of Kilfera Run, Darling District, NSW

note: Griffin's plan on base map printed in red, shows proposed roads, railways, buildings etc., for the central area, Civic to Manuka/Kingston. The Griffin Plan first formalised in 1913 was to produce a flexible modular city design not dominated by artificial or political structures but by natural organic features. Four functions or groups were the basis for the layout - the Government, Military, Recreation and Education Groups. The first two are clearly marked on this map. The Government Group was given central importance to reflect Canberra's role as the national capital with the other groups given auspicious sites capitalising on topography, views and scenery. Municipal, commercial and residential functions fill the spaces in-between. The four Groups are interconnected by a framework of boulevards, business corridors, roads and transit lines. Relief by contours and spot heights. Also issued with: Federal Capital: a report explanatory of the preliminary general plan / by Walter Burley Griffin ; Dept. of Home Affairs, 1914, reissued 1915 (PP 1914-17, v2) Designed by W.B. Griffin in 1913.
mapTitle: Canberra Federal Capital of Australia preliminary plan

note: Sales plan of 18,500 acres of mixed grazing and farming land in Naas and Upper Cuppacumbalong. "18,500 acres of mixed grazing and farming land in 18 blocks from 500 to 1380 acres. Emminently suitable for mixed farming; Crows Lucerne, potatoes etc to perfection.". "Situation-18 miles from Queanbeyan, 2 to 10 miles from Williamsdale railway platform. Close to Canberra.". "Note the easy terms: 5% deposit, 10% on possession, no further payment for 2 years, then 5% annually to completion, with interest at 6%, payable quarterly. Possesion will be given 1st March, 1923.". "Clean sound wool-growing country. Heavy carrying, and drought proof. Permanent running water on each block. Big rich frontages running back into good grazing areas. Two schools on the property.". "Wool from this property has topped the Sydney market.". "A rare chance to secure a good safe living area on extremely easy terms.".

For cottages. £25 deposit, balance in 36 equal monthly instalments including interest at 5 per cent." "Note; All dimensions & easements etc. are subject to registered plan." In left panel: Solicitors to estate. Cox & Wiseman, Crown St., Wollongong. In left panel: Dovers, Beveridge & Moor, Registered surveyors, Wollongong. Text block in centre of map: Braeside is already popular and must increase in value because it is:- (1) Close to North Wollongong Railway Station and princes Highway. (2) On a main bus route. (3) Adjoins an important Public School. (4) Handy to store and Post Office. (5) Handy to High School. (6) Close to new main road bypass roadway (from North Wollongong). Braeside is handy to everything. Braeside is set in delightful surroundings and provides ideal level home building allotments in an area that has made amazing progress during the last 2 years."

note: Photograph (reduced?) of a ms. map by C.T. Madigan extending from Alice Springs (N.T.) to Lake Eyre and Maree (S.Aust.). Also shows topographic detail including streams, swamps, sand ridges, homesteads, bores, wells, margin of artesian basin, railway, rabbit proof fence and state boundaries. Title from note added to photograph. Notes added to map: "A 24/8 ; received 26.1.45 with accompanying letter from Prof. C.T. Madigan (Adelaide)." Stamped on photograph "Records Information & Research Section, Division of National Mapping." A larger version of this map appeared with: The Simpson Desert Expedition 1939, scientific reports, introduction, narrative, physiography and meteorology /by C.T. Madigan. (Transactions of the Royal Society of South Australia ; vol. 69, Part 1, 27 July 1945) Added in ms. to photograph: "see also letter in Rodinga Project File NMP581081."

note: Facsim. copy of map extending from the Western Australian border, Tanami Desert and upper Victoria River region to Tennant Creek and Wycliffe Well. Map shows Buchanan's stock route survey, 1896, to link Kimberley and Victoria River regions with Tennant Creek, including camps, wells and waterholes on the route. Includes notes on topography and vegetation. Relief by hachures. Also shows cadastral boundaries and names of lease holders, streams in the Victoria River and Overland Telegraph Line regions and tracks. Route passed through Green Swamp, to Winnecke Creek and Hooker Creek, to Birrindudu area. Map signed: W.S. Sur. Genl 12/10/[?] W.S. is William Strawbridge. Photograph of an original held by the Northern Territory Archives Service. Imperfect reproduction. Original map has attached newspaper cuttings dated 10/10/1896 and 15/10/1896 from the Adelaide Register, describing the expedition, including reference to notes forwarded to the South Australian Branch of the Royal Geographic Society of Australasia, in 1896. Base map of original is part of a Northern Territory of Australia pastoral map.
